research_question: What is the effect of antenatal magnesium sulphate, compared with placebo, on cerebral palsy in children up to 2 years' corrected age, in offspring of women at risk of preterm birth?
outcome_description: Incidence of cerebral palsy assessed in offspring up to 2 years corrected age, using each trial's reported definition and denominator.
positive_direction: Lower risk or reduced incidence of cerebral palsy in offspring whose mothers received antenatal magnesium sulphate (favoring magnesium sulphate).
search_queries: antenatal magnesium sulphate cerebral palsy randomized trial
magnesium sulfate preterm neuroprotection trial outcome
antenatal magnesium sulphate preterm birth controlled trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials or controlled clinical studies evaluating antenatal magnesium sulphate administration in women at risk of preterm birth compared to placebo or no treatment.
Studies assessing cerebral palsy or related motor/neurodevelopmental outcomes in offspring up to approximately 2 years corrected age.
Studies reporting quantitative outcome data including numbers or rates of cerebral palsy events and group denominators.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, or study protocols).
No comparison between antenatal magnesium sulphate and a control/placebo group.
No quantitative data reported on cerebral palsy or neurodevelopmental outcome from which effect sizes or risk ratios can be derived.
Completely unrelated to antenatal magnesium sulphate administration or pediatric neurodevelopmental outcomes.
moderators_to_extract: Age at pediatric assessment (e.g., 18 months vs. 24 months corrected age)
Primary indication for administration (fetal neuroprotection vs. pre-eclampsia or tocolysis)
Denominator definition used (all live births vs. surviving children assessed at follow-up)
Magnesium sulphate dosing regimen (loading dose and maintenance duration)
Gestational age upper limit at randomization (<30, <32, or <34 weeks)
effect_size_note: Risk ratios (RR) calculated from the raw counts of cerebral palsy cases and the trial-reported total denominator per arm (whether surviving children assessed or all randomized/live births). An RR < 1 indicates neuroprotection (lower risk of cerebral palsy in the magnesium sulphate arm).
